extracted_by: hand, T-0315 — the Democrat read, June 1834
note: Vol. I No. 29, and THE RICHEST ISSUE IN THE MONTH for a reconstruction. Page 3 is NOT interleaved — each segmenter column reads straight down one printed column — which is why the placements the other three issues cut in half are quoted whole here and why this issue is the witness the June reading leans on. Page 4 is interleaved. Pages 1-2 are poetry and foreign news apart from the editorial half of page 2 columns 5-6, which carries the building count and the population estimate. NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST: all twenty-four columns were read, not searched.

claims.normalized: Chicago.—Our Town [is] building up rapidly. Since spring commenced, there has been built [u]pwards of se[v]enty-fi[v]e b[ui]ldings, and among this number we notice some substantial ones of three stories high, and the commencement of two or three others for Stores of three stories. Emigration is still increasing, and has increased one half since last year, having already a settled population of at le[a]st 1500, and the country i[s] filling up in like proportion. Rents are high, and lots rent on the principal street for $300 a foot front. Our commercial business is by no means contemptible.
claims.notes: THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THE JUNE READING, and it is a count rather than an impression: upwards of SEVENTY-FIVE buildings put up in Chicago between the start of spring and 18 June 1834, some of them three storeys, with two or three more three-storey STORES begun. It is the paper's own editorial and not a correspondent's, and it is a year and a fortnight before the scene date, so it measures the town at the start of the boom this reconstruction stands at the end of. The settled population at 1500 and Lake Street ground at $300 a foot front are the same paragraph's. AGAINST T-0313's APRIL WITNESS: 'Seven or eight buildings have been raised in this town within the past week' (1834-04-16), which at that rate for the ten weeks of spring is the same order of magnitude and corroborates it. The interleaving here is column-internal editorial spill and the quote takes only the lines of the paragraph itself; lines 2020, 2023, 2026 and 2028 carry single stray letters from the column beside it and are left out.

placement.offset_normalized: their ware house on South water St. five doors east of the corner of Randolph st.
placement.note: T-0869 RULED THIS PLACEMENT A BEARING, NOT AN ADDRESS. All three printings of this advertisement were re-read at the page images on 2026-09-11 and every one of them sets 'the corner of Randolph st.' — see data/research/newspapers/clark_filer_randolph_corner_1834.json for the readings, the crop regions and the deposit sha256. They are ONE standing setting re-impressed, not three compositions: identical line breaks through the placement, the same 'cosisting' misprint, the same chair cuts, the same 'Chicago, June 10, 1834. 28' at the foot, and the phrase runs in at least five issues from 1834-06-11 to 1834-07-23. So the cross street was NOT mis-set by a slipping hand — there is no per-impression variation to be the slip. What stands is that the firm named a corner it did not stand on, which is how it locates elsewhere in the same month ('three doors from the Baptist meeting house', 1834-06-04). A wrong word in the firm's own copy, standing for six weeks, cannot be separated from that and has the same consequence: the phrase does not measure onto the committed plat. The ware house keeps street_only, `streets_cross` is right to refuse the ordinal (T-0771), and the anchor is left as printed rather than amended to what the plat allows. Do not re-open on a closer reading of these columns; only another impression setting a DIFFERENT street, or a source placing the ware house on the ground, moves it.

claims.notes: READ AT THE PAGE IMAGE ON 2026-09-11 (T-0869). This issue's page 3, column 3 sets 'of Randolph st.)' cleanly, and its tail carries the firm's signature, the N.B. on sign and ornamental painting and the dateline 'Chicago, June 10, 1834.' — the impression the other two are read against. THE PLACEMENT WHOLE, AND UNBRACKETED — this issue's page 3 is not interleaved, so the two words the 1834-06-11 printing cuts ('doors east') are on the page here. Five doors east of Randolph on South Water Street is the tightest offset in the June reading after the Lake Street lot-and-block claim (c006). THE N.B. IS A SECOND TRADE: sign and ornamental painting done by the same firm — which is where a signboard on this street would have been made.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051).
